stage1.impression: A witty, story-led ident with a real idea. A twinkling violet star turns out to be a meteor and punches the planet (a good squash at 0.73 s), and the crater it leaves becomes the mark in the EARF lockup: the animation draws the logo, which is ownable. Everything is built from discs, and the one-colour version translates cleanly (black globe, paper land, bullseye crater). Against it: the first ~0.6 s is effectively a still (a tiny sparkle and meteor; the trace is flat until the hit). The aftermath stacks look-changes in 0.9 s (flash, white puffs, charcoal smoke, scattered crescents, then a four-ring red/orange/yellow/lilac crater), with hairline rings that won't hold small or in one colour. The crater reads as a target or heat-map more than a dent, the globe is generic clip-art, and the wordmark's R has a closed counter, so it reads as a blob next to the slit counters of E and F. The slide-and-reveal (1.6-2.3 s) is the best-timed passage, and the 1.4 s end hold is fine. A good draft with a real idea, not yet a mark to ship.

keep: The story draws the mark: the violet sparkle becomes the meteor, the strike makes the dish, and the meteor stays as its violet core into the lockup (sheet 1 frames 01, 04, 11, 12). One colour thread runs from the first frame to the last, and only this brand could own that motion.

The strike has real weight and follow-through, and the aftermath flows without a stop: a one-frame splat, a two-frame starburst, the planet squashed and knocked along the blow (frame 05, 0.73 s), then a cloud that chars from the middle out and is eaten from inside so the hole opens over the dish (frames 08-10). From 0.72 to 1.61 s the longest still is 0.067 s, and the crater hands straight into the move aside.

changes.problem: The meteor carries the first 0.7 s and the whole story, but it is a speck, so its wind-up and most of its fall don't register and the trace reads the opening as a still.
changes.evidence: Sheet 1 frames 02 (0.43 s) and 03 (0.60 s): a violet dot, then a short comet in the top-right corner, about a twelfth of the planet's width; on ink (sheet 2) it is dimmer still. The trace is flat from 0.00 to 0.60 s (longest still 0.633 s, mean change 0.06 %). The fall first crosses 0.2 % at 0.633 s, two frames before the jump to 1.94 % at the hit (0.70 s).
changes.expected: A violet ball about an eighth of the planet's width, with its lighter leading face readable from the wind-up on. Its flame (2.3 times the ball wide) reads as a real streak, and the trace lifts during the fall instead of only in its last two frames. With ranks 3 and 4, the opening's flat stretch drops from 0.63 s to under 0.5 s. A short settled beat while the sparkle twinkles is right and stays.

changes.problem: Fourteen puffs, eight of them a ring of small ones, make the cloud read as beads or bubble wrap rather than one cumulus. Every puff later becomes a crescent, so the wisps scatter into a dozen curls.
changes.evidence: Sheet 1 frames 06-07 (0.83 s, 1.00 s): small puffs strung round the mass like beads; sheet 3 frames 06-07: an outlined bubble cluster. Frame 10 (1.43 s): about a dozen thin dark crescents round the dish like lashes, which in sheet 3 become a scribble of paper outlines.
changes.expected: Eleven puffs, with five fat, unevenly spaced bumps round the edge instead of eight beads. The total mass is the same (5 x 1.3 squared is about 8 small puffs), and so are the pop, stagger, boil and drift. The black-and-white cloud reads as a few big paper puffs. At 1.43 s there are three fewer wisps and the outer ones are fatter, so the curls round the dish read as smoke, not lashes.

accept.check: Around the cloud's edge there are no more than five small puffs, and none sits apart from the mass like a bead.

changes.problem: After the ting, the sparkle just sits for a tenth of a second before the wind-up starts: a dead gap in an opening that is already sparse.
changes.evidence: Card: ting at 0.24 s, wind-up at 0.34 s. Trace 0.24-0.34 s: 0.02-0.05 % a frame, flat. Frame 02 (0.43 s) still shows the meteor sitting at the sparkle's spot.
changes.expected: The ting launches the meteor: as the long rays reach out, the ball grows out of the sparkle and draws back, and it is falling by 0.36 s. With rank 4, the fall keeps its present 0.226 s (0.36-0.586 s) and its zip. Without rank 4, the fall stretches to 0.326 s and the hit stays at 0.72 s.

accept.check: The sparkle is gone and the meteor has already left its starting point, falling with its flame showing.

changes.problem: The strike comes at 0.72 s, after 0.63 s that the trace reads as still, while cloud, char, wisps and crater must fit into the 0.89 s before the move aside: the opening is too sparse and the middle too crammed.
changes.evidence: Trace: flat from 0.00 to 0.60 s, then 0.72-1.61 s never under 0.2 % for more than two frames (mean 0.71 %). The white cloud gets only 0.30 s before it chars at 1.02 s, and is at full size for about a tenth of a second (frames 06-07 at 0.83 and 1.00 s).
changes.expected: The strike lands at 0.62 s, 0.1 s sooner. The white cloud the owner asked for gets 0.40 s before it chars at 1.02 s, about 0.2 s of it at full size, so it reads as a stage of its own; it keeps boiling and drifting, with no new stop. Nothing from 1.02 s on moves, and the ident still runs 3.76 s. Make this change only together with rank 3: on its own it would cut the fall to 0.126 s.

changes.problem: The wisps take 0.42 s a puff, so the last crescents vanish just as the planet starts to move aside. The finished dish, the payoff the owner asked for ('then the crater is visible'), never stands clean on the full-size planet, and the busiest stage lingers.
changes.evidence: Frame 10 (1.43 s) is still full of crescents. The trace decays slowly from 0.63 % at 1.40 s to 0.11 % at 1.57 s, with only two frames under 0.2 % before the move aside at 1.61 s. By the card, the outermost puff finishes at 1.02 + 0.12 + 0.05 + 0.42 = 1.61 s.
changes.expected: The same wisps curl the same way, but the last one is gone by about 1.49 s. The dish's last wobble and the core's bounce and cooling then play on a clean planet for about 0.12 s before the move aside (if the move follows the smoke instead, the ident ends 0.12 s sooner).

accept.check: No smoke crescent remains on the planet: only the sea, the land, the dish and its core.

changes.problem: The ripples run out to 1.3 rad, where their foreshortened arcs lie parallel to the planet's lower-left edge, so the globe reads as a plate (a rim round a shallow well) rather than a ball.
changes.evidence: Sheet 1 frame 11 (1.60 s): two or three hairline arcs running parallel to the lower-left edge, about a quarter of the radius inside it; they build through frames 08-10. Sheet 3 frame 11: the same arcs as paper hairlines on the black planet.
changes.expected: The three rings spread round the dish across the open Atlantic and die out well inside the planet's lower-left edge (their far side passes about 0.45 of the radius from the centre). They read as water, and round a speaker as sound, and never trace the planet's outline.

accept.check: No thin line runs parallel to the planet's lower-left edge, so the planet does not look like a plate with a rim.

changes.problem: The third ripple runs until 1.87 s, so thin rings are still crossing the planet a quarter-second into the move aside, which puts detail where the hand-off should be clean.
changes.evidence: Frame 11 (1.60 s), one frame before the move aside, still shows ripple arcs travelling. By the card, the third ring starts at 1.02 s and runs 0.85 s.
changes.expected: With rank 6, the rings travel at about the same speed (about 1 rad a second) over a shorter distance and are all gone by 1.57 s (1.47 s with rank 4). During the move aside, only the dish's cooling core is still changing on the planet.

accept.check: No ripple ring is left on the planet.

changes.problem: The shock ring runs out to 1.95 rad, so for most of its life it hugs the far limb as a light hairline just inside the planet's edge. Against the squashed, knocked silhouette, it reads as a doubled outline.
changes.evidence: Sheet 1 frame 06 (0.83 s): a thin light line just inside the left and lower edge, out of step with the squashed outline. Sheet 3 frame 06: the same as a paper hairline inside the black edge.
changes.expected: The shock still sweeps over land and sea and still wraps the near (upper-right) limb, so the planet still reads as a sphere, but it dies on the face of the planet about 0.8 of the radius out on the lower left. No second contour.

accept.check: No thin light line runs just inside the planet's left or lower edge.

most_important: Rank 1, meteor 0.085 -> 0.12. The meteor carries the first fifth of the ident and the whole story (sparkle, meteor, core). At its current size the trace reads the first 0.63 s as a still, which is where the owner's 'not fluid or quick enough' begins. If two more changes are allowed, make ranks 3 and 4 together: launch it on the ting and strike 0.1 s sooner.
out_of_scope: The dish as drawn reads as a target or heat-map in colour, and as a bullseye (even an eye) in black and white (frame 11; sheet 3 frame 12), not plainly as a loudspeaker. A hint of the surround's roll, or a highlight on the cone, would make it a speaker. This matters because the dish is the brand's whole point (horn loudspeakers), but the planet's drawing is fixed.

The R in the EARF wordmark renders without a counter: a solid bowl with only a notch at the baseline (frame 12 on all three sheets). Next to the open counters of E, A and F it is the darkest letter and will blob at small sizes. The wordmark and hand-off are shared and fixed; check whether this is the master artwork or the renderer.

The shared hand-off leaves 1.47 s flat at the end (2.27-3.73 s, 39 % of the ident). Together with the opening, it makes the whole feel slower than the owner wants (round 23). It is fixed for every ident; a 1.0 s hold is worth considering at house level.
The globe is a generic flat Earth (Americas facing, emoji-like), so all the distinctiveness sits in the dish. Fixed.
The owner's order (white cloud, then black wisps) runs opposite to a real blast (fire, black smoke, pale dust). It reads fine as a cartoon, so nothing here works against it.
for_owner: Black-and-white wisps: on the solid black planet, black smoke can only show through its paper gaps, so over the sea the wisps read as paper scribbles (sheet 3 frame 10, 1.43 s). Accept outline-only wisps in black and white, or let the smoke turn to the ground colour where it crosses the sea?

What the quicker smoke (rank 5) should buy: a held beat on the clean dish before the move aside (the move stays at 1.61 s), or a shorter ident (the move follows the smoke at about 1.49 s, and the ident runs about 3.64 s).

Round a loudspeaker dish, three concentric ripples read as sound as much as water. Is that double meaning wanted? If so, keep three rings and their tight spacing; if not, two rings read more plainly as water.
